claims.text: THE FULL PROVENANCE CHAIN, WHICH THE NODE SHOULD CARRY. John Greenewald Jr wrote to 341 CS/SCBR at Malmstrom AFB on 9 May 2001 requesting all documents pertaining to a 16 March 1967 incident in which there was a malfunction of missile silos. Headquarters 341st Space Wing replied on 14 June 2001, over the name Marty S. Stephens, stating that it had received the request on 18 May 2001 and was releasing copies of excerpts and supporting documents of the 341st Strategic Missile Wing histories for 1 Jan to 31 Mar 1967, 1 Apr to 30 Jun 1967, 1 Jul to 30 Sep 1967, 1 Oct to 31 Dec 1967 and 1 Jan to 31 Mar 1968, adding: 'We do not have any audio or video tapes, or documents of any personnel injured.' Fees were waived and the requester was referred to NARA.

The shutdown message is cited as Msg, (S) DM 02752, SAC to 341 SMW, subject 'Loss of Strategic Alert Echo Flight, Malmstrom AFB', 17 Mar 67, Ex 43. NEITHER DOCUMENT IS IN THE RELEASE AND NEITHER HAS BEEN OPENED BY THIS BOARD.

desc: Excerpts from five quarterly histories of the 341st Strategic Missile Wing, Malmstrom AFB, released to John Greenewald Jr by Headquarters 341st Space Wing on 14 June 2001 and posted by The Black Vault. The January to March 1967 volume carries a section headed 'the investigation of Echo Flight incident and the results' at pages 32 to 40, footnoted throughout to a single classified engineering report of 23 March 1967. The release is the document the board's Malmstrom node names as decisive. It states the shutdown happened and states that the UFO reports around it were disproven, and it names no launch officer on duty.

timeline.label: The engineering investigation reports it cannot determine a cause
timeline.text: The Engineering Investigation Team's 'Report of Engineering Investigation of Echo Flight Incident, Malmstrom AFB, Mont. - 16 Mar 67', dated 23 March 1967 and classified Secret, is the document the entire Malmstrom controversy turns on. It is footnoted on almost every page of the wing history's Echo Flight section and has never been opened by this board. Through the history it states: 'The investigation teams at Malmstrom, were unable to determine a logical cause for the incident.'
